title: Kain DCC Parity Matrix
description: Machine-readable parity inventory for the shared native DCC shell plus KSculpt and KPainter target surfaces.

status_definitions.label: Reference Only
status_definitions.summary: The capability exists in the reference baseline but does not yet have a Kain-owned implementation seam.

status_definitions.label: Scaffolded
status_definitions.summary: Kain has a real owning surface, registry entry, or prototype seam, but the feature is not yet close to parity.

status_definitions.label: In Progress
status_definitions.summary: The feature has active Kain-owned implementation work and should be treated as a moving target.

status_definitions.label: Implemented
status_definitions.summary: The feature exists in Kain-owned code with a durable owner, but full parity acceptance is not yet claimed.

status_definitions.label: Validated
status_definitions.summary: The feature exists in Kain-owned code and has an explicit validation hook that proves the parity claim.

domains.label: Shared Native DCC
domains.summary: Capabilities shared by both sculpt and painter lanes, including desktop workflow, session state, and shell ownership.

domains.label: KSculpt Parity
domains.summary: Reference features sourced from .reference/sculpting/* and their Kain-owned parity status.

domains.label: KPainter Parity
domains.summary: Reference painter features sourced from .reference/graphos/* plus current Kain painter scaffolds.

features.label: Native desktop dev loop
features.summary: One-command native desktop iteration with app materialization, child launch, root watching, and rebuild-on-save.

reference_sources.note: Hot reload should feel like the old TS workflow, but for native desktop software.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Dev loop entrypoint, file watch, debounce, and child lifecycle.
CLI command surface for native-ui dev.

features.notes: The loop is real today, but the flagship DCC app still needs host hardening and broader scenario coverage.

features.label: Hot reload versus restart classification
features.summary: Compatible edits hot-apply in process, while incompatible changes restart the host from persisted artifacts.

reference_sources.note: Native hot reload must be as credible as the TS workflow.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Compatibility metadata and artifact role classification.
Runtime reload and transfer of reload-safe state.
Reload decision application in the operator loop.

features.notes: The classifier exists now; the remaining risk is host stability and DCC-specific state restore semantics.

features.label: Registry-owned native workbench shell
features.summary: Workspace modes, rails, docks, panes, tools, and status chrome live in app registries instead of host-local logic.

reference_sources.note: The UI system should be at least as robust as the original React shell.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Docked workbench shell and pane semantics.
Workspace mode registry.
Tool and lane catalog.

features.notes: The registry-driven shell exists, but parity-grade sculpt and paint benches are still incomplete.

features.label: Shared session document and runtime snapshot
features.summary: Sculpt and painter state should round-trip through one durable session contract and runtime snapshot surface.

reference_sources.note: One shared DCC session and asset contract is required for parity.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Canonical session schema.
Reducer-owned session mutations.
Materialized runtime-side state projection.

features.notes: The session surface exists, but sculpt and painter parity state still needs to be folded into one contract.

features.label: Undo, redo, and restore-safe session recovery
features.summary: User-visible authoring history and restore paths should survive compatible reloads and restarts.

reference_sources.note: Undo and redo controls are part of the primary operator chrome.
Timeline and layered paint editing imply durable state recovery.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Reducer-owned transition seam.
Command routing seam for future history integration.

features.notes: The shell and reducer seams exist, but a unified parity-grade history model is not landed yet.

features.label: Machine-readable parity capability inventory
features.summary: Every parity claim should have a stable feature id, owner, reference source, and validation hook.

reference_sources.note: Task 1.1 requires an explicit parity matrix and capability inventory.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Canonical matrix manifest for DCC parity.
Validator and reporting entrypoint.

features.notes: This tranche lands the baseline inventory; future work should wire the matrix into live shell capability status and benchmarks.

features.summary: Brush selection, adjustable radius and intensity, and additive or subtractive sculpt modes.

reference_sources.note: Brush arsenal, radius and intensity sliders, and KADD or KSUB toggles.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Clay sculpt and voxel rebuild tools.
Brush radius, strength, and falloff pipeline defaults.

current_kain_surfaces.note: Viewport mode contract for sculpt workflows.
Viewport interaction posture and transform defaults.

features.label: Transform gizmo, space switching, and snap policy

current_kain_surfaces.note: Universal gizmo profile and transform defaults.

features.label: Sculpt layers, visibility, and merge operations
features.summary: Layered sculpt ownership with visibility, active-target selection, merge-down, merge-selected, and merge-all behaviors.

features.label: Clay and PBR preview modes, matcaps, and geometry export
features.summary: Sculpt preview materials, matcap selection, and visible-result export such as glTF.

CLAY versus PBR mode switch plus project materials.
glTF export and visible-layer export are first-class actions.

Texture and packed export receipts.
Preview material and shader ownership map.

features.label: Primitive authoring, mesh ingest, and export receipts
features.summary: Primitive creation, mesh import, active edit-target binding, and geometry export receipts.

reference_sources.note: Primitive loading and storage import live beside the sculpt workspace.
